# [ABSOLUTE] Non-negotiable constraints

- **Language:** respond in English at all times.
- **Runtime:** Laravel Herd on native Windows. **No Docker, no Sail, no WSL.** Never emit `./vendor/bin/sail`.
- **CLI:** run commands yourself from the project root; never ask the developer to paste output.
  - `php artisan <cmd>` · `composer <cmd>` · `vendor/bin/pint` · `php artisan test --compact`
- **Frontmatter path convention:** the canonical skills live in `.opencode/`. Every reference below is
  written as `.opencode/...`; `.claude/` and `.cursor/` are generated copies with the same content.

# [MUST] Read the matching skill before writing code

| Task                                                      | Read                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Any backend or frontend change (security applies to both) | `.opencode/skills/owasp/SKILL.md` (portable core, always-on) + `.opencode/skills/owasp/STACK.md` (this stack's bindings) |
| PHP / Laravel / business logic                            | `.opencode/skills/backend-php/SKILL.md`                                                                                  |
| Directory structure, layers, module layout                | `.opencode/skills/backend-php/SKILL-ARCHITECTURE.md`                                                                     |
| Vue / Inertia / Pinia / PrimeVue / Tailwind               | `.opencode/skills/frontend/SKILL.md`                                                                                     |
| Frontend directory tree, file placement                   | `.opencode/skills/frontend/SKILL-ARCHITECTURE.md`                                                                        |
| New feature, non-trivial or ambiguous scope               | `.opencode/skills/SSD/SKILL.md` — 7-phase spec-driven flow                                                               |
| Simple FLAT CRUD scaffolding                              | `GUIDE/module-make.md` + `stubs/architecture/`                                                                           |
| Deciding whether to extract, abstract or duplicate        | `.opencode/skills/PRINCIPLES/SKILL.md`                                                                                   |

If a skill covers the task, read it first. No exceptions.

**What exists today:** `src/Modules/` is **empty** — no domain module is implemented. The architecture
suite in `tests/Architecture/` is therefore intentionally vacuous (it skips itself), and
`resources/js/generated/` holds only a `.gitkeep`. `src/Shared/` is populated. Never claim a module,
screen or DTO exists because a rule above names it.

# [MUST] Judgement calls — the short form

The full treatment, with sources and enforcement, is `.opencode/skills/PRINCIPLES/SKILL.md`. These
six lines are the ones an agent gets wrong most often:

- **Rule of Three.** Two occurrences are a coincidence; extract on the third. Extracting on the second
  is YAGNI wearing a DRY costume.
- **DRY is duplication of _knowledge_, not of code.** Two copies of a business rule = a fail. Two
  copies of a shape with no shared rule = leave it alone.
- **A class nothing references is a presumptive feature** (Fowler): it costs construction _and_
  delay, even when the prediction is right, and it will get in your way.
- **PROGRESSIVE is an OCP bet.** Uncle Bob called the OCP "a big lie … that depended upon prescience
  and perfect foresight". That is why the de-escalation rule exists, and why it carries a date.
- **Small is not the goal.** A big module with a small interface beats three small modules with
  three interfaces. A wrapper that only forwards its own arguments is dumb (Henney) and shallow
  (Ousterhout) — both now a failing test.
- **Separate only along a boundary you can name. If you cannot name it, leave it local.** An agent
  that splits a coherent unit across nine files loses the ability to see it at all.

And the reframe that matters most for an agent: **skipping a layer is a decision with a reason, not
an omission.** Omitting it because it was not required is compliance, not a shortcut.

# [MUST] Backend

- No business logic in controllers. Validate with `FormRequest` or Spatie `Data`.
- **Response shapes are Spatie Data** (`{Entity}Data::from()` / `::collect()`) for Inertia props _and_ JSON.
  There is no `JsonResource` in new code. A `JsonResource` subclass is a FAIL.
- **N+1 prevention is mandatory.** Enable `Model::shouldBeStrict()`. List queries use
  `with('rel:id,fk,col')` with explicit columns; aggregates via `withCount`/`withSum`/`withAvg`;
  relation+filter via `withWhereHas`.
- Every route authorized: `auth` + Spatie `permission:*` or a Policy. UUID routes use `->whereUuid()`.
- Audit trail: `Spatie\Activitylog\Models\Concerns\LogsActivity` with explicit `logOnly([...])` +
  `logOnlyDirty()` + `dontLogEmptyChanges()`. Never `logAll()`, never log secrets/PII.
- When the UI exposes row selection, ship **both** bulk delete and bulk restore, with matching routes.
- Argon2id hashing. CSP via `spatie/laravel-csp`. Headers via `bepsvpt/secure-headers`.

# [MUST] Frontend

- `<script setup lang="ts">` on every `.vue`. No Options API in new code.
- **ZERO `any`** — no `any`, no `as any`, no implicit `any`, no `@ts-ignore`. Use `unknown` + a narrowing guard.
- **Backend types are GENERATED.** `php artisan typescript:transform` emits
  `resources/js/generated/generated.d.ts` from the Spatie `Data` classes. Hand-writing an interface
  that mirrors a backend `Data` class is a FAIL — it is exactly how `any` and drift creep in.
- **Vue 3.5 APIs are mandatory, not optional:** `useTemplateRef<T>()` · `useId()` for generated ids ·
  destructured props with defaults (**`withDefaults` is banned**) · `defineModel<T>()` for every
  custom `v-model` · `onWatcherCleanup()` in any watcher that starts a timer/request · `defineSlots<T>()`.
- **Server state → Pinia Colada. Client state → Pinia setup stores. Never mix.**
  Every query declares both `staleTime` and `gcTime`; paginated lists use `placeholderData: (prev) => prev`.
- UI primitives only through **Volt** components in `src/volt/` (`@/volt/*`). No other UI library.
  Volt components are code-ownership copies — edit their `pt` pass-through config, never inline classes
  at the call site.
- Toasts: `Toast` + `useToast()`. `<Toast />` must be mounted once. Forms: `@primevue/forms` + Zod v4.
- Theme toggling uses ONLY the `.dark` class on `<html>`. The `dark:` variant is bound via
  `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))` in `app.css`.
- **No hardcoded colours** — no hex, no `bg-red-600`, no `bg-[#hex]`. Use `var(--token)` or the
  PrimeUI bridge classes (`bg-primary`, `text-surface-700`).
- Animation: Vue's native `<Transition>`/`<TransitionGroup>` first. Volt overlays already animate —
  do not re-wrap them. Reach for `motion-v` only for layout animations, gestures, or scroll-linked work,
  and lazy-load it (it is ~125 kB raw).

# [MUST] Codebase exploration

**`codebase-memory-mcp` is the primary structural navigation tool.** Check the graph before introducing
anything new.

1. `codebase-memory-mcp` — symbols, callers/callees, impact, boundaries
2. `Read` — only after the graph identified the file
3. `grep` / `Glob` — exact text, or when the graph can't answer

**Delegate the exploration, not the decision.** Graph payloads are large and are re-sent every request.
Run them inside a subagent (`codebase-memory-scout` for orientation, `codebase-memory` for
task-directed, `codebase-memory-auditor` for impact/dead code) so only the conclusion returns.

Never invent modules, files, classes or routes. Coverage is best-effort — `check_index_coverage` for
every cited path and re-verify with `grep` before any negative claim ("there is no X").

**Known blind spots:** routes are runtime closures the indexer cannot resolve — read `routes/*.php`
directly. Blade views are opaque nodes; a view is NOT evidence of a backend feature.

**`vendor/` and `node_modules/` are never the answer to a question about this app.**

| Question                        | Source                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Installed PHP package + version | `composer show`                                                        |
| Installed JS package + version  | `package.json`                                                         |
| How a package's API works       | **Context7**, scoped to the installed major                            |
| Where something lives here      | `codebase-memory-mcp`, then `app/`, `src/`, `resources/js/`, `routes/` |

# [MUST] Module finalization — the closing gate

A change is **not done** until the gate exits 0. Two tiers — pick by what you touched.

## Tier 1 — every module, every refactor (safe)

```bash
npm run module:done
```

| #   | Step                       | What it proves                                                 |
| --- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0   | `php artisan config:clear` | the analyser and the app see current config, not a stale cache |
| 0b  | `php artisan doctor`       | 26 environment diagnostics — see below                         |
| 1   | `npm run format`           | Prettier applied                                               |
| 2   | `npm run syn`              | `.claude/` and `.cursor/` regenerated from `.opencode/`        |
| 3   | `npm run types:check`      | `vue-tsc --noEmit` — zero type errors                          |
| 4   | `npm run build`            | Vite production build succeeds                                 |
| 5   | `composer analyse`         | PHPStan + Larastan level 5 — zero errors                       |
| 6   | `composer pint:test`       | Pint style **including `--blade`** — zero pending fixes        |
| 7   | `php artisan test`         | Pest suite green                                               |

**Reading the output.** `laravel/pao` (dev dep, first-party) swaps the output of `pest`, `phpstan`,
`rector` and `artisan` for compact JSON **when it detects an agent**, and leaves it alone for humans.
So: a green run is green, do not re-run a failing step hoping the wording changes; quote a failure
verbatim from the structured fields rather than paraphrasing it; and never treat "it printed no
error" as evidence — **the exit code is the verdict.** See `owasp/STACK.md` §17.

`laravel/pao` also means a "skipped" Pest test prints as skipped rather than vanishing. A suite that
is entirely skipped has passed _vacuously_ — check the skip count before reporting green. Today the
module tests in `tests/Architecture/` are all skipped by design, because `src/Modules/` is empty.

### `laravel/doctor` — the agent sanity check

First-party (MIT, announced Laracon US 2026). It exists because agents write code well and are **bad at
noticing the environment broke underneath them** — a missing PHP extension, a stale env key, a config
that no longer loads. Step 0b catches exactly that class of failure.

```bash
composer doctor          # the gated run (one diagnostic excluded, see below)
composer doctor:all      # everything, no exclusions
php artisan doctor --fix            # deterministic fixes
php artisan doctor --format=agent   # machine-readable, for an agent to parse
```

> **Excluded: `Laravel\Doctor\Diagnostics\SqliteDatabaseExists`.** False positive on Windows in v0.1.0 —
> it builds the path as `base_path()` + an already-absolute path, yielding
> `C:\...\aquashield\C:\...\aquashield\database\database.sqlite`. Verified 2026-09-27: the file **does**
> exist and `is_file(config('database.connections.sqlite.database'))` is true. **Never run
> `doctor --fix` for it** — it would create a junk directory. Drop the exclusion once fixed upstream;
> `composer doctor:all` exists so you can check.

### `laravel/vet` — review `vendor/` before it lands

`laravel/vet` (MIT) is a **Composer plugin**. Every update drops code into `vendor/` that nobody on the
team has read. `vet` makes that reviewable and records trust per package version **plus file hash**, so
a later update only asks about what actually changed. A package nobody has trusted exits non-zero,
which makes it enforceable in CI.

```bash
composer update:safe                   # review the pending update's diffs (interactive)
./vendor/bin/vet --init                # trust what is installed, write vet.json
./vendor/bin/vet --fresh               # clear the trust file and re-seed
./vendor/bin/vet --plan=composer.json  # audit a composer plan file
```

`vet.json` is committed and currently trusts **219 packages**. Two options that matter:

| Option                    | Effect                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--minimum-release-age=N` | with `--init`, hold back any release younger than N days — a direct defence against a freshly-published malicious version (OWASP A03) |
| `--from=X --to=Y`         | show the delta between two versions instead of the trusted one                                                                        |

Requires `allow-plugins: { "laravel/vet": true }` — already set.

## Tier 2 — only when a `Data` class, enum, model or controller changed

```bash
npm run module:codegen      # = composer codegen  +  the Tier 1 gate
```

```
php artisan ide-helper:models --write    # rewrites model docblocks
vendor/bin/pint                           # ← MUST run after it, see below
php artisan typescript:transform         # regenerates resources/js/generated/generated.d.ts
php artisan scramble:clear && scramble:export && scramble:cache
```

> **⚠️ Order constraint — `ide-helper:models --write` must always be followed by `pint`.**
> ide-helper writes a `@property` block that Pint's `phpdoc_separation` rule rejects. Run the two in
> the other order and they ping-pong forever: ide-helper rewrites, Pint reverts, and the gate never
> converges. This is why `composer codegen` embeds `@pint` immediately after it, and why Tier 1
> deliberately does **not** call ide-helper at all. Verified 2026-09-27 by running the pipeline twice.

**`typescript:transform` reads the classes by reflection, not the docblocks** — so it is
order-independent w.r.t. Pint. The Frontend types come from the Spatie `Data` classes; that is the whole
reason not to hand-write them.

`resources/js/generated/` must exist or the transformer throws. It ships with a `.gitkeep`.

### PHPStan level 5 is a ratchet, not a ceiling

`phpstan.neon` analyses `app`, `src/Modules`, `src/Shared` and `database` at **level 5**, with a comment
saying "raise it module by module". That is a policy with no mechanism behind it, so state it plainly:
**level 5 is global and stays 5 until someone deliberately raises it.** Raising it is a dated,
reviewed change with its own PR — never a side effect of touching a file, and never silenced with
`@phpstan-ignore` to make a gate pass. `src/volt/*` is excluded because PHPStan cannot read `.vue`.

With `src/Modules/` empty, step 5 currently analyses `app` and `src/Shared` only. That is the honest
state, not a passing check of the whole codebase.

While iterating:

```bash
vendor/bin/pint --dirty        # in-flight formatter, modified files only
composer analyse               # PHPStan alone
npm run test:module -- Booking # only the module's tests
composer test:tia              # Pest 5 TIA replay — see the note below
npm run types:watch            # vue-tsc in watch mode
npm run dev:async              # vite + vue-tsc together
```

Then **re-index the graph** — an MCP call, not a shell command:

```
index_repository(repo_path: "C:/Users/Lenovo/Herd/aquashield", mode: "full")
```

`mode: "full"` is the closing gate; `fast` is only the in-flight refresh. Verify with `index_status`:
nodes/edges must have moved and `indexed_at` must be newer than your last source edit.

Editing a method _body_ without changing what it calls does not need a re-index. Adding, renaming or
deleting any symbol, route, or `implements` always does.

**Never report a module complete on a partial run.** If a step fails, say so with the real output.

### Pest 5 TIA — opt-in fast inner loop, never the gate (verified 2026-10-18)

`composer test:tia` runs `vendor/bin/pest --tia`: the first run records which files each test
touches, and every later run re-runs only the tests affected by your changes while replaying cached
results for the rest. It is an **inner-loop** tool:

- **The closing gate stays `php artisan test` — a full run.** Never put `--tia` in the gate or on a
  CI command, and `pest()->tia()->locally()` is deliberately **not** set in `tests/Pest.php`: there is
  no CI here, so "locally only" would include the gate.
- **Currently inert on this machine — two prerequisites left (checked 2026-10-18).** The repo exists
  (`git init`, branch `master`) but has **no commit yet**: Pest stops with `Tia mode requires at least
one commit`, because the baseline is anchored to a revision. It also needs a coverage driver —
  Herd's `…\herd\bin\php85\ext` ships no `xdebug.dll`/`pcov.dll` and `php.ini` loads neither. Until
  both are in place, use `php artisan test`; nothing else depends on TIA.
- **Storage is outside the repo:** `~/.pest/tia/<project-key>/`. After large refactors, re-record with
  `vendor/bin/pest --tia --fresh`.

### Known gate state — read this before blaming your change (as of 2026-09-28)

The gate is **red on arrival**, for reasons that predate any module work:

| Step                                                              | State                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syn:check` · `format:check` · `types:check` · `build` · `doctor` | green                                                                |
| `analyse` (PHPStan L5)                                            | **27 errors, all in `src/Shared/`**                                  |
| `pint:test`                                                       | **23 files, all in `src/Shared/` + `resources/views/app.blade.php`** |
| `php artisan test`                                                | green — 20 tests, 7 skipped (the module assertions)                  |

The PHPStan errors are carried over from a previous application, not written here: a dangling
`App\Models\CompanyData` that no longer exists, dead `catch (FailoverableException)` blocks, four
traits used zero times, and a batch of `??` offsets that PHPStan can prove are never null. They are
real findings and they are **not** fixed by any config change.

What that means for you:

- Do **not** "fix" a gate failure by lowering the PHPStan level, adding a baseline, or adding
  `@phpstan-ignore`. All three are explicitly banned above.
- A new module must be clean **on its own files**. `phpstan analyse src/Modules/{Module}` and
  `pint --test src/Modules/{Module}` prove that without the inherited noise.
- Clearing the `src/Shared` backlog is a separate, deliberate task. Do not fold it into a module
  commit.
- `tests/Architecture/` is a real testsuite (added 2026-09-28) and **was silently missing from
  `php artisan test` before that** — which is why `7 skipped` is the honest count and not a
  regression. If a suite disappears from the count, check `phpunit.xml` before assuming green.

# Working on the skills themselves

- `.opencode/` is the **canonical source**. `.claude/` and `.cursor/` are **generated**.
- `npm run syn` regenerates the mirrors. `npm run syn:check` fails if they drifted — it is part of `verify`.
- Never hand-edit a mirror; the next `syn` overwrites it.

# [SHOULD] General quality

Mobile-first on every UI component. `font-family: var(--font-sans)`. Prefer descriptive names over comments.
